unit.why: A homily from Divrei Shmuel on joyful repentance versus sadness, with one short memorate in which the author's father rebukes him for being sad; the anecdote is wrapped in a teaching frame.

stories.summary_en: Expounding 've-atah al te'atzvu' to mean that repentance must come with joy, the author gives his grandfather's sign for telling a broken heart from sadness. He recalls that his father once rebuked him harshly for his sadness, more than for worse faults, because sadness is never repented of. He adds sayings of R. Mordechai of Lechovitch and R. Aharon that sadness is itself a sin, like anger.

tags.why: Mainly exegesis and ethical teaching; the short anecdote is embedded in it
